rationale: Chronic inflammatory signaling commonly increases during human immune aging.
TNF-alpha signaling via NF-kB is elevated across aged immune cells in large human single-cell atlases.
Older human circulating immune cells show increased inflammation- and senescence-associated expression.
Senescent immune states are associated with increased secretory inflammatory programs; older human B cells show increased senescence and SASP markers.
Aging is associated with diminished B-cell function, antibody responses, and B-cell receptor repertoire diversity.
Reference gene set is fetched from the curated Reactome pathway REACTOME_TCR_SIGNALING; no genes are manually selected.
